source.analysis: The saved brief specifies match fidelity and confirms ownership. Key landmarks are the slim cream header, oversized two-line serif headline with italic second line, generous hero whitespace, rotated sage square with an arch and outlined oval, thin ochre divider, editorial service rows, sage studio-note band, and compact footer. These are reconstructed as live HTML and CSS, with Aster Nail Studio and Toronto bound to saved business information. Services use one runtime-repeated template rather than the reference’s stale offering. Both selected photos appear in a paired editorial gallery within the service section, keeping the reference’s abstract hero intact. On mobile, the same hierarchy stacks deliberately. Booking and management buttons use trusted runtime bindings; the appointment link navigates to services, and the studio note expands natively to show live hours.
limitations: The reference’s exact font is unavailable; system Georgia and Arial approximate its typography, with some differences in letterforms and text width.
Including both selected photos and all saved services makes the service section taller than the reference; the photo gallery is an intentional addition.
The second photo contains black bands. Its gallery crop removes those bands while retaining the hands and foliage.
The decorative hero artwork is recreated with CSS rather than an original vector file, so gradient and curve contours may differ slightly.
Booking availability and confirmation are supplied by Luster’s runtime; this source does not implement a separate booking backend.
